d.d: The logic function exclusive OR (as opposed to inclusive OR), whose output is true only when exactly one of its inputs is true.
The connective "exclusive or". One way to state its meaning in plain English is "if either A or B, but not if both."
d.x: The XOR of (0,0) is 0; (0,1) is 1; (1,0) is 1; and (1,1) is 0.

d.d: A logic gate that implements "exclusive or".
To perform the XOR function upon.
